title: Fibroblast Derived Human Engineered Connective Tissue for Screening Applications
protocol: Warm fibroblast growth medium (FGM) to 20-25 °C.
Thaw cryopreserved cardiac fibroblasts in a water bath at 37 °C for approximately 2 min until only a small amount of ice is left.
Transfer the cell suspension dropwise into an appropriate sterile centrifuge tube containing 10 mL of FGM using a 2 mL serological pipette.
Rinse the cryovial with 1 mL of FGM and transfer it to the centrifuge tube for optimal cell retrieval.
Resuspend cells in FGM using a serological pipette with a bore tip to minimize cell damage by shear stress.
Centrifuge the resuspended cells at 300 x g for 5 min at 20-25 °C if the DMSO content is high, then carefully aspirate the supernatant.
Swirl the tube to dislodge the pelleted cells and resuspend them in FGM for seeding.
Seed 0.5 x 10^6 cells in 12 mL of FGM into a T75 cell culture flask or adjust the number of cells based on the labware used to maintain a seeding density of 6.7 x 10^3/cm^2.
Replace FGM every other day for 5 days or until cells reach 80% confluency.
Warm FGM, PBS (Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺-free), and cell dissociation reagent to 20-25 °C.
Aspirate the medium from the cultured cells.
Wash cells with 6 mL of PBS and aspirate.
Add 6 mL of the cell dissociation reagent to the cells.
Incubate for 3 min at 20-25 °C until the cells start visibly detaching.
Neutralize enzymatic activity by adding 6-12 mL of FGM to the dislodged cells in the cell dissociation reagent.
Gently pipette up and down 4-8 times using a 10 mL serological pipette.
Transfer cells into a fresh 50 mL collection tube.
Verify the yield with the help of a microscope and a hemocytometer or an automated cell counter according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 x g for 5 min at 20-25 °C.
Aspirate the supernatant and flick the tube to dislodge the pellet.
Resuspend the cells in FGM at 20-25 °C to obtain a cell suspension of ≥ 15 x 10^6/mL.
Strain the cell suspension through a 40 µm mesh cell strainer.
Recount the cell number after straining.
Assess cell viability using an automated cell counter by electrical current exclusion.
Alternatively, use trypan blue dye exclusion test for cell viability assessment.
Proceed with ECT preparation immediately after assessing cell viability.
Dissolve DMEM powder in ddH2O (134 mg/mL) under constant rotation at 37 °C for 1 hour.
Sterilize the prepared DMEM by filtration.
Store the DMEM stock at 4 °C for up to 14 days or -20 °C for up to 12 months.
Dilute a 10x DMEM stock solution to prepare 2x DMEM and add 20% (v/v) FCS in sterile ddH2O.
Optionally, add antibiotics such as penicillin at 200 U/mL and streptomycin at 200 mg/mL.
Pre-chill a 50 mL centrifuge tube on ice.
Add the different components listed in Table 2 to the pre-chilled 50 mL centrifuge tube, avoiding air bubble formation.
Pipette the acid soluble-collagen type 1 hydrogel using a serological pipette with a wide bore tip.
Adjust the salt content of the collagen solution by adding 2x DMEM while gently mixing.
Neutralize the pH by adding 0.2 M NaOH while gently mixing until phenol red indicator turns from yellow to red.
Add cell suspension dropwise into the mixture while gently mixing.
Mix the entire suspension by gently pipetting up and down only once, using a serological pipette with a wide bore tip to avoid bubble formation and minimize shear stress.
Gently swirl the tube 10 times to ensure complete mixture.
Keep the 50 mL centrifuge tube containing ECT hydrogel mixture on ice throughout the casting process.
Pre-wet a 1 mL pipette tip with ECT hydrogel mixture.
Distribute 180 µL of ECT hydrogel evenly into each mold of the 48-well casting plate.
Ensure that the entire plate is completed within 15-20 minutes.
Avoid excessive shear forces during distribution to maintain collagen matrix integrity.
Form a complete loop within each mold.
Do not apply the mixture discontinuously, as it may prevent complete ECT ring formation.
Avoid pipetting into the inner well of the mold.
Prevent bubble formation during pipetting for homogeneous and functional tissue formation.
Carefully place the 48-well casting plate inside the cell culture incubator and let the ECT hydrogel mixture reconstitute for 15-30 min.
Add 600 µL of 37 °C warm FGM per well, without pipetting the culture medium directly onto the forming ECT.
Incubate for 24 h.
Replace the medium every day thereafter with 500 µL of FGM until analysis.
Assess ECT compaction by measuring cross-sectional area.
Use a stereo microscope to record macroscopic images of the top and side views of the ECT.
Perform a line scan analysis using an image processing program.
Trace and measure the ECT diameters at a minimum of 6 positions per arm in each imaging plane.
Calculate the mean diameter from top and side view planes.
Calculate the cross-sectional area according to an elliptic area equation.
Image the 48-well casting plate under a recording device equipped with an integrated area scan camera.
Place the recording device at a fixed distance from the plate.
Use a high-resolution (≥ 5 mega-pixels) monochrome image sensor for imaging.
Employ a near-UV (~390 nm) light source to maximize contrast.
Utilize telecentric lenses if available, to minimize image distortions.
Alternatively, capture macroscopic bright-field images of single wells or the complete plate.
Include a scale bar in the bright-field images for analysis.
Measure the distance between the poles from daily records using an image processing program.
Automate pole detection by running recorded images through software capable of detecting high contrast bright pixels on a dark background.
Calculate pole deflection based on the variation of poles' distance compared to the initial distance at day zero.
Harvest ECT by pulling the stretcher, including ECT, out of its well using forceps.
Hold the stretcher on its base and slip the ECT over the stretcher tips using a fine hook or pipette tip.
Transfer the ECT onto two hooks clamped to the stationary arm and the transducer arm of an extensional dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) rheometer.
Place the DMA rheometer in a custom-made organ bath filled with PBS at 37°C.
Set the rheometer to apply uniaxial tension at a constant linear rate of approximately 1% of the initial distance between the hooks per second.
Use a constant stretching rate of 0.03 mm/s with typical ECT dimensions.
Tare the transducer before initiating the stretch.
Initiate the stretch and record until the point of ECT rupture.
Record macroscopic pictures of ECT before tensile testing.
Calculate CSA (cross-sectional area) required for data normalization.
Process stress-strain analysis and CSA calculation using spreadsheet software.
Analyze force values (mN) per ECT by its CSA to obtain stress values (kPa).
Plot stress values against strain on a XY graph.
Adjust the initial length of the tissue, L0, manually before stretching begins.
Calculate each strain point value using the provided equation.
Use stress value at selected L0 for background subtraction when plotting data.
Determine different biomechanical parameters from the stress-strain curve.
Identify the toe, elastic, and plastic regions on the stress-strain curve.
Locate the yield point in the elastic region before microfracturing begins.
Measure tissue elasticity at the strain corresponding to the yield point.
Define the plastic region between the yield point and failure point.
Determine the ultimate strain at the sudden drop in stress indicating tissue rupture.
Calculate tissue extensibility using the strain value at the failure point.
Identify the maximum strength as the highest stress before tissue breaks.
Measure resilience by calculating the area under the curve up to the yield point.
Assess toughness by determining the area under the curve to the failure point.
Plot a linear regression of the elastic region's linear part for each curve.
Extract XY values (strain and stress) for the yield, failure, and maximum stress points.
Calculate Young’s modulus from the slope of the elastic region's linear segment.
Use a statistical program to compute the area under the curve (AUC).
Determine resilience up to the yield point using the trapezoidal method.
Set the baseline to zero for AUC calculation.
Consider only peaks above the baseline that are at least 10% of the distance from the minimum to the maximum value in the Y-axis.
Determine toughness up to the failure point using the trapezoidal method.
